fullText:
Dodgers pitcher Tyler Glasnow pitched in a game for the first time in 80 days on Tuesday, starting a minor league rehab assignment with the Class-A Ontario Tower Buzzers. Glasnow struck out one in two scoreless innings to open what figures to be a lengthy rehab assignment and a hopeful September return to Los Angeles.

Glasnow needed only 16 pitches to record his six outs on the road against the Lake Elsinore Storm, a San Diego Padres affiliate. He induced a pair of swinging strikes, and got three groundouts, a fly out, and a pop out.

Tuesday was the first game for Glasnow since suffering back spasms during a May 6 start in Houston, which was cut short after only just one inning. Two days later he was placed on the injured list, and was moved to the 60-day injured list on June 6.

If and when Glasnow might return to the Dodgers, he'll join a rotation with an altered depth chart. The Dodgers on Sunday traded for Tarik Skubal, who nestles into the top of the list alongside Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Blake Snell is making his fourth and expected final rehab start on Tuesday night for Triple-A Oklahoma City, with an expected return to the Dodgers next week. Shohei Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3, and the Dodgers are taking things slowly with his left knee inflammation, while still expecting him to be ready come October.

"We're as confident as we can be that [Ohtani's] going to be back and he's going to start throwing soon and building back up," Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said Sunday at Dodger Stadium. "You can never perfectly predict the future, but if you said, 'Hey place a bet on it,' I would be very confident placing it that he will be back pitching.

"I guess from my standpoint, I really hope we get to the end of the season and everyone's healthy and feeling good and strong. That's the best kind of tough decisions and figuring that out that we could possibly have, and we could welcome it."

title: MLB trade deadline winners and losers: Dodgers, Cubs and Padres all go big, while the Mets sell nearly a third of their roster
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers now have Tarik Skubal. The Boston Red Sox now have Adley Rutschman. The New York Mets now have a fully open calendar for October.
fullText:
Another MLB trade deadline has come and gone, with every contender in MLB making some sort of addition at the expense of the teams embracing reality.

It will be a long time before we understand the full ramifications of these trades due to the volatility of prospects, but no day on the MLB calendar shows which way the wind is blowing more than deadline day.

The Los Angeles Dodgers now have Tarik Skubal. The Boston Red Sox now have Adley Rutschman. The New York Mets now have a fully open calendar for October.

Let's dive into what all of this means, starting with the team that will be the talk of baseball well beyond the 2026 season.

If the Detroit Tigers were going to admit defeat and trade Tarik Skubal, the Dodgers loomed as the inevitable destination. And not for a boorish "The Dodgers get EVERYBODY!" reason.

There were basically four, maybe five teams good enough this season to justify giving up the price of two top-100 prospects and more that the Dodgers paid: the Dodgers, the Milwaukee Brewers, the Atlanta Braves, the Tampa Bay Rays and maybe the New York Yankees or Red Sox. Of that group, only the Dodgers, Brewers and Rays really had the prospect depth to make the deal happen.

The thing is, though, the Brewers and Rays usually need those prospects in a way the Dodgers don't. Those teams build their contenders via affordable pre-arb and arbitration talent, with free agency as an occasional indulgence. Meanwhile, Zyhir Hope, the crown jewel of the Dodgers' prospect package was — and we're not joking here — the third-best outfielder on L.A.'s Double-A team, according to most prospect rankings, behind Josue De Paula and Mike Sirota.

All of that left the Dodgers without another legitimate suitor to compete against. They paid a completely reasonable (but still considerable for a rental) price, Hope and two high-risk, high-reward pitchers in River Ryan and Brady Smith, in exchange for maybe the one guy available at the deadline who could have meaningfully improved their World Series odds.

They didn't stop there, either. Despite a comically large rotation depth chart, especially with Eric Lauer and Emmet Sheehan not being traded, L.A. still went for Royals starter Kris Bubic, a 2025 All-Star who is currently on the injured list but could be useful down the line.

And with Will Smith and Dalton Rushing both now on the injured list, the Dodgers brought in familiar faces Ben Rortvedt and Hunter Feduccia, who can at least offer an improvement on their worst-case scenario at the position.

No organization in all of sports combines resources, competence and the urge to bathe in the blood of your enemies quite like Andrew Friedman's front office. It was no different at this year's trade deadline.

The Dodgers might have made the biggest splash, but the crown for most total value added at this year's deadline belongs to the Cubs, who overhauled a rotation that badly need overhauling.

The team had already acquired David Peterson from the New York Mets, and the left-hander has been more than solid outside of a bizarre meltdown early last month. Then they got Kevin Gasuman from the Toronto Blue Jays, Clay Holmes from the New York Mets and Braxton Garrett from the Miami Marlins.

Gausman should offer instant impact. Holmes was the Mets' most reliable starting pitcher before he fractured his right fibula in May, but his return from the injured list is imminent. Garrett has looked promising in the past, though he's still trying to find his footing after undergoing internal brace surgery in 2024.

Chicago also landed reliever Ryan Zeferjahn from the Los Angeles Angels and outfielder Tyrone Taylor from the Mets, filling two other notable needs.

This team is definitely better than it was a couple of days ago, and it wasn't cheap, with top-100 prospects Jefferson Rojas and Moisés Ballesteros among the several prospects leaving the organization. It probably won't be enough to nullify the Brewers' 6.5-game lead in the NL Central, but this squad suddenly looks like by far the best wild-card team in the NL.

Never change, A.J. Preller. We really do mean that.

For the past few years, the San Diego Padres have been seeing the bill come due. They once had one of the most enviable collections of young talent in baseball (maybe the most enviable other than their neighbors to the slight north), but that has deteriorated through a series of win-now trades.

Now, the Padres sit at 58-54 entering play Monday, which is a vast improvement on where they were 10 games ago, and they're one game out of a competitive wild-card race. They have a minus-12 run differential. Their high-priced core is visibly aging.

So, of course, they bought again.

This time, San Diego improved a bad rotation by bringing in Robbie Ray from the San Francisco Giants and Casey Mize from the Detroit Tigers, sending away the No. 2, 4 and 9 prospects in a weak system, according to MLB Pipeline.

The Padres will remain competitive this season. They will have more questions to answer in the offseason, when top starter Michael King likely opts out and Ray and Adrian Morejon hit free agency.

That's for future Preller — or, and we say this ominously, someone else — to figure out.

It's refreshing to see a Pirates team try, even from 3.5 games out of the last wild-card spot entering Monday.

Pittsburgh ranks second in MLB in runs scored and seventh in runs allowed. There's enough talent in the rotation that the bullpen was clearly the place for improvement, and improve they did.

In deals for Luke Weaver from the Mets, Kirby Yates from the Angels and Lake Bachar from the Marlins, the Pirates bought as hard in the bullpen as any team at the deadline this year.

This is still a team with holes, and one that definitely needs to pray Paul Skenes' recent velocity issues are a temporary nuisance. And yet, this is now Pittsburgh's best chance in years to end a decade-plus playoff drought.

Remember when we said there were four or five teams good enough to have reason to acquire Skubal? Let's go through what those teams did.

The Dodgers obviously did a lot. The Brewers added rotation help with Dustin May and bullpen help with Antonio Senzatela and JoJo Romero. The Rays added a much-needed catcher in Liam Hicks and a classic reclamation project in former All-Star starter Freddy Peralta. The Yankees got some real bats in Luis Garcia Jr. and Heliot Ramos. The Boston Red Sox went for it with the Rutschman blockbuster (more on that later).

The Braves, meanwhile, have a haul headlined by fourth outfielder Lane Thomas. They got a salary dump in Tyler Mahle and minor-league depth in Bailey Falter. They got Brent Suter and Tyler Uberstine, relievers who hardly scream "confident innings in October."

The Braves overall have been excellent this season. Only the Dodgers have better odds to win their division than Atlanta. But, uh, what's the plan once you're facing the Dodgers and their gatling gun of multi-million-dollar arms?

The answer to that can't be "well, the Dodgers are going to win anyway," like some fans will say. Fire any executive who says that. Success is fleeting in MLB, and you can't treat a 100% playoff team like a bonsai tree, making only the most delicate of tweaks, while all the other heavy hitters slam the buy button.

Atlanta obviously isn't done for, but there's no way to describe this deadline as anything better than a disappointment for president of baseball operations Alex Anthopolous.

The Red Sox are going for it! It is legitimately thrilling to see a team go from dead in the water to one of the deadline's biggest buyers, even if Boston's second-biggest acquisition, infielder Curtis Mead, immediately fractured his wrist.

But let's talk about that Rutschman deal.

Rutschman isn't quite the superstar he looked like he would be when he first reached MLB, but he's still one of the game's better catchers and under team control for 2027 too. Boston is probably going to love him.

As for the price general manager Craig Breslow paid for him, let's go to a talent evaluator quoted by Sean McAdam of MassLive.com: "I'm absolutely dumbfounded by this...This is literally one of the most ridiculous trades I've seen in 30 years."

In exchange for a season and a half of their new catcher plus another catcher in Jake Rogers, Boston sent away pitching prospect Anthony Eyanson (their No. 2 prospect at MLB Pipelin), pitching prospect Kyson Witherspoon (No. 4), outfield prospect Enddy Azocar (No. 5), current back-up catcher Carlos Narváez and a player to be named later.

The baseball world is prone to overrating the value of prospects, but that's still a considerable price for a guy whose median outcome is a quality starter and not much more.

Yes, we just talked about what a haul the Orioles got for Rutschman. It was a good deal, but also one that showed all the bad building up under the supposed mastermind in Baltimore.

Remember 2023? The Orioles won 101 games, they still had the best farm system in baseball, they were about to get a new owner in David Rubenstein who was supposedly willing to spend in a way the Angelos family never did. And at the center of it all was Mike Elias, the former Astros player development lead who was demonstrating the power of alchemy in Baltimore.

What happened next might be the most stark example of a would-be contender failing to take a step forward in recent memory. The Orioles never had the pitching to back up their enviable collection of hitting talent, and then all that hitting talent collectively took a step backward. They went from 101 wins in 2023 to 91 in 2024 to 75 in 2025. They are on pace for 78 wins in 2026, with a farm system that was middling before that infusion of talent from Boston.

The Rutschman trade represents the final stretch of a cycle. Elias appeared incredibly adept at the first part of the cycle, building up talent without having to care about the results on the field. He proved disastrous at the next leg, waiting for a contender to assemble itself in front of him. And now he's sending away the vanguard of that first wave of talent for fuel for the next lap.

There is little evidence the next ride will be any different, but at least Elias is doing what he loves again.

Moving back to the Dodgers, not everyone in that building will have reason to be pleased with what they've done.

Consider the case of Justin Wrobleski, who has been a pleasant surprise in his first year as an MLB starting pitcher. He entered Monday ranked 11th in MLB in ERA while ranking behind only Yoshinobu Yamamoto in innings pitched for the Dodgers. He made his first-team All-Star team last month, and would be one of the most valuable components of nearly any other MLB organization.

He is also likely to be pitching out of the bullpen this postseason if everyone is healthy. As is Roki Sasaki, who is suddenly fulfilling his potential as one of the most-hyped pitching prospects in MLB history. The Dodgers are undefeated in nine appearances by Lauer and he is one injured list return from falling out of this rotation. Sheehan got optioned like 10 minutes after the trade deadline.

In an organization with Skubal, Yamamoto, Shohei Ohtani, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, it's not enough to be good for a season. We're just not sure how any young pitcher is supposed to accomplish more than that in this monstrosity of an organization.

We didn't really expect anything different, but the New York Mets have officially pulled the plug on the most disappointing season in MLB.

With Holmes, Peralta, Taylor, Weaver, Huascar Brazobán, Brooks Raley, A.J. Minter and Rortvedt, the Mets traded away eight players over the past two days. That is 31% of an MLB roster. They got back some decent talent overall, but that's not the win they wanted this season.

It's not a full rebuild in New York, but it's at the very least a moment for reflection. This team was supposed to be Dodgers East with David Stearns running the show with a near-unlimited checkbook, but little has gone right since their magical playoff run in 2024.

title: Best pitching rotations in MLB: Where Dodgers' group led by Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto ranks
description: Here's the rundown on which MLB teams have the best starting pitching rooms with the latest Skubal trade.
fullText:
Best pitching rotations in MLB: Where Dodgers' group led by Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto ranks originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

After the Los Angeles Dodgers finally landed Tarik Skubal following more than a year of trade rumors, the rest of Major League Baseball was put on notice as the league's best team added one of its best pitchers.

The Dodgers now have as many combined Cy Young and MVP awards on their roster (10) as the rest of the National League combined. However, Los Angeles isn't the only team with an elite starting rotation.

Four other clubs rank among the top five starting pitching staffs in baseball, while several strong rotations just missed the cut.

Here's a look at the MLB teams with the best starting rotations following the Skubal trade.

MORE: Tracking news and rumors from the 2026 MLB trade deadline

When at full strength, no team comes close to matching this Dodger lineup 1 through 5. For most teams around the MLB, any one of these pitchers would be their ace. With Snell and Glasnow still on the IL, the Los Angeles pecking order has featured Emmet Sheehan and Roki Sasaki, along with the occasional bullpen game.

Prior to Skubal's arrival on the team, the Dodgers had the league's fourth-best team ERA at 3.60, according to ESPN. Hitters bat on average .216 against the Los Angeles entourage, which is the MLB's lowest mark, along with only 414 total runs against (2nd). Just hours before the MLB trade deadline hit the final bell, the Dodgers traded for Kansas City Royals starting pitcher Kris Bubic, who is still on the IL with a left elbow injury. With yet another deep playoff run looking imminent in the City of Angels, their pitching is a key reason why. Anything other than a World Series trophy hoist for the third year in a row would be a colossal failure for this group.

MORE:Full details of Dodgers' trade for Tarik Skubal

Coming in at the second spot in the MLB's best starting pitching lineups is the New York Yankees. While outfielder Aaron Judge has the biggest name in the Yankee organization, their pitching room is among baseball's best. The AL powerhouse has a league-low 3.30 cumulative ERA, along with the third-lowest opponent batting average of .225.

Since returning from Tommy John Surgery, Gerrit Cole picked up right where he left off. In his last seven starts, the right-handed flamethrower has pitched at least five innings and notched five or more strikeouts. In front of him stand Max Fried and young phenom Cam Schlittler. The Yankees are widely thought to be the American League's top contender despite currently sitting 3.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East's No. 1 spot.

MORE: Who did the Yankees trade for IF Luis Garcia Jr.?

While the Brewers seem to fall short every year despite a stellar regular season, they've consistently had a strong group of starting pitchers to put them in contention. This year, Jacob Misiorowski has put his name on a pedestal as one of the sport's top arms. The 24-year-old currently tops the MLB charts with 190 strikeouts through 21 games (nine per game), along with throwing a large portion of the fastest pitches in the modern era.

Brandon Woodruff has again fallen victim to injuries, with his latest being a season-ending shoulder surgery. Kyle Harrison is set to return soon after a stint on the 15-day IL with left forearm tightness. Logan Henderson and Brandon Sproat, a young pitcher who was landed in the Freddy Peralta trade with the New York Mets, round out a fine lineup that has a high likelihood of propelling the Brew Crew to another deep postseason run.

While the Tampa Bay Rays have been without Ryan Pepiot for the duration of the 2026 season, Shane McClanahan has picked up another injury after missing the entire 2024 and 2025 campaigns with Tommy John surgery and another elbow procedure. Regardless, Drew Rasmussen and Nick Martinez have held down the fort before the team added Freddy Peralta in a trade with the Mets.

While Griffin Jax was one of Team USA's brightest spots at this year's World Baseball Classic, the 31-year-old struggled to begin this season as a bullpen option. He was eventually moved into one of the team's starting positions and has since recovered well. In his last four outings, Jax has gone more than five innings and recorded six or more strikeouts. Tampa Bay currently boasts the sixth-lowest ERA across the majors (3.68), along with the fourth-lowest opponent batting average (.228).

MORE: Grading the Tarik Skubal trade

Rounding out the MLB's top pitching staffs is the Boston Red Sox. Despite Garrett Crochet being on the IL since April 29 with left shoulder inflammation and still not having a throwing timetable, the Red Sox have ranked quite well in pitching statistics for the 2026 season. Boston currently has the third-lowest team ERA in the MLB (3.53), along with a league-low 410 runs allowed.

Outside of Crochet's misfortunes, Sonny Gray has been nothing short of stellar this season. The journeyman has rekindled the potential from his early MLB career and has tallied a 13-2 record as of August 2, second only to Philadelphia Phillies ace Cristopher Sanchez. Behind Gray stands offseason acquisition Ranger Suarez, who has had an up-and-down 2026 season (4-3, 3.15 ERA, 105 K's), and the young duo of Payton Tolle (6-6, 3.30 ERA, 110 K's) and Jake Bennett (6-4, 2.74 ERA, 46 K's).

title: Blue Jays reportedly trade Kevin Gausman to Cubs, signaling sell-off months after World Series appearance
description: The deal in part signals a Blue Jays selloff at the MLB trade deadline, months after they took the Dodgers to extra innings in Game 7 of the World Series.
fullText:
The Toronto Blue Jays have traded starting pitcher Kevin Gausman to the Chicago Cubs, signaling a sell-off at the MLB trade deadline months after they took the Dodgers to extra innings in Game 7 of the World Series.

The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Mitch Bannon reported the trade on Sunday, hours before Monday's 6 p.m. ET trade deadline. In return, according to the report, the Blue Jays will receive outfielder Brett Bateman and infielder Ty Southisene, both prospects.

The move in part cements a season of disappointment for the Blue Jays, who started 2026 with hopes of competing for the AL East title and returning to the postseason. Instead, they've entered the stretch run in last place in the division at 52-60 with long-shot hopes of competing for a wild-card spot.

Whether the Blue Jays would be sellers at the deadline or hold steady for a shot at the postseason was unclear before the All-Star break. But they lost five of their first six games coming out of the break, including three to the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays.

Gausman is playing on the final season of a five-year, $110 million contract. He was a prime candidate for a deadline deal to a contending team seeking a contributor with an expiring contract.

A two-time All-Star, Gausman isn't at his peak form at 35 years old. But he's been a reliable starter for much of his career, including this season as one of MLB's leaders in starts and innings pitched.

Gausman provides the Cubs with a mid-rotation option days after they designated veteran Jameson Taillon for assignment.

Taillon, 34, was in the midst of a career-worst season with a 5.92 ERA and 25 home runs allowed. Chicago traded Taillon to Toronto in a separate deal earlier Sunday for cash considerations or a player to be named later.

Taillon pitched 76 innings for the Cubs this season, and his departure left Chicago with a hole in their rotation. Gausman, who's made 14 postseason appearances, slots in for what the Cubs hope is an upgrade for the stretch run and a likely playoff appearance.

The Cubs leave a 2-1 loss to the Yankees on Sunday at 63-49, in control of first place in the NL wild-card standings with a four-game cushion over second. They're 6.5 game behind the Brewers for first place in the NL Central.

Per MLB Pipeline, Southisene ranked as Chicago's No. 13 prospect, and Bateman rated at No. 21. Neither are in MLB Pipeline's top 100 overall prospects. They're both now building blocks for Toronto's future.

The Los Angeles Dodgers made headlines late Saturday night when they acquired back-to-back Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers.

title: How Dodgers’ aggressive pursuit of Tarik Skubal led to deadline stunner: ‘Skubal or nothing’
description: Where there’s smoke, they say, there’s usually fire. And on Saturday, as signs first publicly emerged that the Dodgers were making a move in the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, the team’s...
fullText:
Where there’s smoke, they say, there’s usually fire.

And on Saturday, as signs first publicly emerged that the Dodgers were making a move in the Tarik Skubal sweepstakes, the team’s behind-the-scenes talks with the Tigers were indeed reaching a fever pitch.

A day earlier, the organizations had begun discussing a trade for Skubal — the American League’s reigning two-time Cy Young Award winner and this year’s top deadline target — in earnest for the first time.

“Right before the first pitch, I heard that it was pretty much done,” Roberts recounted on Sunday, as the rest of the baseball world was still digesting the Dodgers’ latest blockbuster acquisition. “There were obviously things that had to go on with medicals, so it wasn’t actually even finalized. I just heard that it was pretty much close.”

Over the next three hours, the Dodgers successfully pushed the deal across the finish line, ironing out a package that included three minor-league prospects — outfielder Zyhir Hope, and pitchers River Ryan and Brady Smith — in exchange for the majors’ most dominant pitcher over the last three seasons.

“Being on our side, you didn’t really know how long the process was gonna go, whether it was gonna go into Sunday, into Monday,” Friedman said. “But, obviously, we were of the mind to be aggressive and try to get a deal done.”

A day later, the reverberations of the trade were still rattling throughout the baseball industry, most of which had never bought the Dodgers’ repeated Skubal-related bluffs in recent weeks.

Though the team had insisted publicly and privately that it didn’t need Skubal, and that it wouldn’t make an all-in push to get the pending free agent at inflated deadline prices, rival teams always saw the Dodgers as his most likely landing spot.

The expectation was that Friedman & Co. would make a strong push in pursuit of a third straight World Series championship.

Friedman and Roberts effectively confirmed that on Sunday, saying the club had decided early on to target the 29-year-old superstar, whom they felt was the one true “needle-mover” on this year’s deadline market.

“Skubal or nothing” was the way Roberts put it.

“Our mindset,” Friedman added, “was we’re going to be really aggressive for one player.”

That didn’t mean the Dodgers were certain they would get Skubal.

As recently as the start of this week, it was unclear if the Tigers would even move their star pitcher as they began clawing their way back in the playoff picture. On Thursday, one team source estimated only a 25% likelihood of a deal.

But after Detroit blew a 7-0 lead in what became Skubal’s Tigers finale on Wednesday, a trade finally started to feel like an inevitability.

And over the next 72 hours, the Dodgers didn’t just hang around “the backboard,” as Friedman has quipped about so many of their other star additions over the last half-decade.

This time, armed with a war chest of prospects and few other roster holes to fill, they wanted to try to box everybody else out.

“With where our core is this moment in time,” Friedman said, “erring on the side of aggressive made the most sense right now.”

The first signs of apparent movement came just as the Dodgers began their Saturday night game against the Red Sox, when their Double-A affiliate in Tulsa scratched the highly touted Hope (who is the team’s No. 4 prospect and widely ranked as a top-50 talent around the sport) as well as fellow outfielder prospect Kendall George from their lineup.

Sources initially described that decision as precautionary — the Dodgers playing it safe with two young talents as trade deadline conversations intensified.

But internally, a Hope-centric package had already taken shape.

(An aside: George was also believed to be the subject of trade discussions the Dodgers were having with clubs, but a source noted he was also dealing with a knee issue, having only come back from a freak injury earlier this season).

At that point, the Dodgers were seeking medical records and doing “due diligence,” according to two sources. The Post’s Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman also reported that the team’s package was believed to be topping those of fellow Skubal contenders, including the Brewers and Yankees.

“Stay tuned,” one person with knowledge of the team’s plans said.

The Dodgers had maintained interest in other players throughout the process, according to sources.

One contingency was Mets starter (and former Yankees closer) Clay Holmes, who could have been a swingman for a Dodgers team that could use reinforcements in the bullpen. The team was reviewing reports for other pitching targets, too.

Still, Skubal remained their primary focus, with Friedman indicating the Dodgers never seriously engaged with any other teams about potential alternatives. And at some point during Saturday’s game, a final deal was struck including two young pitching pieces from the Dodgers’ well-regarded farm system.

That none of the Dodgers’ active big-league arms were included came as a surprise.

There had long been an assumption that the Tigers would want someone from their current rotation, with Emmet Sheehan coming to be seen as the likeliest candidate.

That’s why, when Sheehan was conspicuously absent from the Dodgers’ dugout during the middle innings of their eventual Saturday night loss, industry speculation piqued. It’s not unusual for starters to return to the clubhouse on days they aren’t pitching. But on this occasion, it fueled growing rumors he was headed out the door.

Instead, as Sheehan said from his locker after the game, no one had informed him of any pending trade situation.

Rather, the Tigers ultimately agreed to Ryan (the uber-talented but often-injured 27-year-old right-hander who has been sidelined by a hamstring problem in Triple-A) and Smith (a raw-but-promising 21-year-old flamethrower who has yet to climb above Single-A).

That rounded out what rival evaluators described as a modest — albeit, for what is still a rental player, understandable — package that the Tigers hope includes plenty of long-term upside.

“We gave up a lot of talent,” Friedman insisted. “Those guys are really good.”

But for what the Dodgers hope is the final piece of their three-peat puzzle, they were more than happy to oblige for another marquee transaction.

“Whenever there’s a star-level player that is available that can really shift championship odds,” Friedman said, “those are the moments that we’ll be more aggressive.”

title: Dodgers visit Tigers Aug. 28-30: Will Tarik Skubal pitch in series?
description: Whether Tarik Skubal pitches against the Tigers at Comerica Park later this month will depend on manager Dave Roberts' starting pitching plans.
fullText:
Tarik Skubal will return to Detroit later this month, and not just to pick up his belongings.

The Los Angeles Dodgers play the Tigers at Comerica Park on Aug. 28-30, which will mark the return of Detroit's now-former ace and two-time reigning Cy Young winner.

Skubal was traded from the Tigers to the Dodgers on Sunday in a blockbuster move ahead of Monday's trade deadline.

Skubal, 29, is expected to make his first start for the Dodgers against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field on Tuesday. The question Tigers fans want to know: Would that put him line to start against Detroit at Comerica Park?

The simple answer is: Stay tuned.

If he starts Tuesday and the Dodgers stick to pitching him every five games, then he would just miss the Tigers series (assuming the Dodgers don't have any rainouts). But the Dodgers also have three days off between now and then, so if they decide to pitch Skubal every five days, then he would be in line to start against the Tigers, the team that drafted him in the ninth round of the 2018 draft and developed him into one of the best pitchers in the game.

If Skubal pitches every five games: Tuesday at Cubs, Aug. 10 vs. Royals, Aug. 15 vs. Brewers, Aug. 21 vs. Pirates, Aug. 27 at Braves

If Skubal pitches every five days: Tuesday at Cubs, Aug. 9 at Diamondbacks, Aug. 14 vs. Brewers, Aug. 19 at Rockies, Aug. 25 at Braves, Aug. 30 at Tigers

Of course, the Dodgers could do a combination of both days and games between starts for Skubal. If they value making his starts at Dodger Stadium (why wouldn't they), the every-five-games scenario lines up much better.

Skubal made his last start for the Tigers at Comerica Park on Wednesday, allowing three runs on four hits in 6⅔ innings against the Baltimore Orioles in a game the Tigers lost, 10-9, in 12 innings after leading 7-0.

Skubal left in the seventh inning to a standing ovation from Tigers fans.

title: Tarik Skubal breaks silence on Dodgers trade with so much emotion
description: Tarik Skubal had to fight back tears when it came time for him to talk about the Dodgers and Tigers trade.
fullText:
Of course Tarik Skubal was going to be emotional after the trade that sent him to the Los Angeles Dodgers (check out our trade grades of this one). The Detroit Tigers have been his Major League home since 2018, when the franchise took him in the ninth round of the 2018 MLB Draft.

He's pitched seven seasons with the big club and won two Cy Youngs, and it seemed like the Tigers were moving into contention last year. Sadly, it wasn't the same this season, and with Detroit not giving him a well-earned contract extension, the Tigers had to get something back before he headed into free agency.

As you'll see, he spoke to reporters early on Sunday morning and talked about the various emotions he was going through. Although he was excited to head to the Dodgers, Skubal talked about the failure to bring a World Series to the organization.

Then, he spoke about his now-former teammates whom he's best friends with, and you could hear his voice waver. Then, he needed a moment to collect himself before moving on to talk about his excitement surrounding joining the Dodgers.

title: Dodgers Lose Struggling Reliever to Injury Amid Bullpen Shuffle
description: The Dodgers made a roster move on Aug. 1, promoting Kyle Hurt back to the major league staff in favor of Cole Irvin.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made a roster move on Saturday, Aug. 1, promoting Kyle Hurt and Wyatt back to the major league staff, designating Cole Irvin for assignment, and most notably, putting Will Klein on the injured list.

Klein is hitting the 15-day injured list with right elbow soreness. The righty had a noticeable drop in velocity of a couple of miles per hour from the start of the season, which is a sign of wear.

His pitching results have also been trending down.

In June, he had a 4.32 ERA in 8.1 innings. Things got worse in July; he had a 7.71 ERA in 9.1 innings.

Manager Dave Roberts noted that the team was going to find out the cause behind the drop-off.

“We’re still trying to dig into it,” Roberts said. “I thought there were some good fastball throws in there tonight, but the secondary stuff, that’s kind of what’s getting him.

“The sweeper is not a strike; is not getting chase from it. The curveball has a different shape to it than it did last year. So I don’t know if it’s an arm thing, a mechanics thing, but that’s something we’re trying to dig in on.”

Irvin was brought in for a bullpen game on Friday as Shohei Ohtani stopped pitching due to left knee soreness, leaving an opening in the six-man rotation.

The Dodgers deployed Edgardo Henriquez as the opener, Will Klein as the piggyback, and then Irvin, who threw six valuable innings and 102 pitches.

He saved the Dodgers from using their regular bullpen arms, with only Evan Phillips pitching after the lefty finished his work.

Now, Irvin heads back down to the minor leagues, something he was well aware would be his fate.

“Part of the job. I signed up to be a Major League Baseball player, and some nights aren’t going to go your way,” Irvin said.

“And you just got to be able to take it on the lip and keep going. I can sit here and smile because all the work that I put into my season so far got me this opportunity, and I’m not going to let anything get in the way of the joy that I have right now. And yeah, it sucks to lose, but at the same time, I earned this opportunity.”

Since getting demoted, Hurt has pitched in three games. He has allowed six runs in 2.1 innings of work.

Much of that damage came in one appearance, when he allowed two hits, two walks, and a hit batter that led to five runs being charged to him.

Hurt was sensational for the Dodgers in the first few months, showing promising stuff and looking like the pitcher that the organization had been raving about.

However, over time, things fell apart, but he gets another shot to prove that it was an aberration rather than his actual level of play.

title: Assessing the Dodgers trade deadline priorities
description: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across MLB. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dodgers fans and fans across the country. fullText:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across MLB. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Dodgers fans and fans across the country. 

What do you get the team with the most talent in the sport? We asked you guys, and a new catcher was at the top of the wishlist, taking 47 percent of the votes. Before getting into what that might entail, let’s take a moment to appreciate the absurdity that not a single vote was cast for a position player (outside of catcher) — rightfully so, with no open spot on this roster the team could realistically hope to improve on That and other priorities, of course, while trying to improve its World Series odds.

The remaining 53 percent who didn’t vote for catcher were nearly split between starting and relief pitching. Both units share the exciting prospect of reinforcements on the way or recently arrived, with Edwin Díaz just activated and Blake Snell not far behind him. While any bullpen could always use an extra arm, the starting staff has this looming cloud over it with questions regarding the availability of Shohei Ohtani.

Assessing options on the market for these positions of “need,” with Will Smith’s rehab finally showing promising signs, the Dodgers may very well limit themselves to less splashy options. As we covered before here, Victor Caratini and Ryan Jeffers of the Twins may represent the best targets. A pending free agent, Jeffers wouldn’t cost a king’s ransom, unlike other more exciting controllable catchers, and the veteran Caratini would represent a safety net type of acquisition.

On the starting pitching front, with Eric Lauer thriving since being acquired by the Dodgers and Snell returning, it feels like a Tarik Skubal or bust kind of situation. Sure, there are other options who could prove to be an improvement over what the Dodgers have on the backend of the rotation right now, at least in terms of ceiling, but they’re not particularly likely moves. Unfortunately for the Dodgers, some of the better potentially available relievers at the deadline play for the Padres, making for a difficult deal as San Diego would inevitably prefer to move them to someone else. Everyone might want to talk about Mason Miller as the dream target, but pending free agent Adrian Morejón might be a more feasible acquisition and a great one in his own right.

Whether the target is a starter or a reliever, perhaps the best team to talk with is the Mets. While their record is atrocious, the Mets don’t lack in high-end reliever quality, with Brooks Raley and Luke Weaver pitching great and firmly available. A.J. Minter was also in this group, but he was the first to go, traded to the Twins on Thursday night. In the unlikely scenario the Dodgers want to add a starter not named Skubal, Clay Holmes ticks a lot of boxes, having recently returned from an injury and heading for the open market at the end of the year.

title: Dodgers pull Shohei Ohtani from lineup as knee problem sparks new concerns
description: Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, who has been dealing with knee ailment, will not start in the team's series finale against the Seattle Mariners.
fullText:
In the latest twist in Shohei Ohtani’s battle with left knee discomfort, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts held him out of the lineup Thursday against the Seattle Mariners.

Ohtani reported soreness Wednesday night in his left knee, which he treated over the All-Star break with a lubricating orthovisc injection and rest. So the Dodgers’ training staff recommended a day off.

“I expected him to play,” Roberts said. “I appreciate him saying that there’s some soreness to then allow me to make a decision of what is in his best interest, and that’s what we’re doing.”

Roberts said he’s “very confident” that Ohtani will be in the lineup Friday when the Dodgers open a three-game series against the Boston Red Sox.

But the Dodgers previously believed only pitching aggravated the injury. Ohtani hasn’t pitched in a game since July 3, and he hasn’t thrown off a mound in a little over a week. He’s been running through weighted plyo ball drills to keep his arm in shape without putting pressure on his knee.

It raises questions about how to best manage Ohtani for the rest of the season.

“I’m trying to restrain from a forecast of what’s going to happen, as opposed to just reading and reacting,” Roberts said. “Three days ago, we just had an off day, and to say there’s some soreness certainly is different than what we’ve done the last two weeks. Is it a trend? I hope not. But if it is, then we just got to manage it.”

Roberts said he didn’t believe any specific incident Wednesday aggravated Ohtani’s knee.

“The last couple days he’s been on base a lot more,” Roberts said. “So I think that’s been a good thing in one sense, whereas the last part of the road trip he wasn’t, so there might have been a little something to that.”

Ohtani also mentioned earlier this week that his biceps problem, which flared for the second time this season during his last at-bat July 3, has not completely subsided. But the Dodgers have downplayed the severity of that ailment and are under the impression that throwing doesn’t hurt it.

When asked if the team would consider shutting down Ohtani for 10 days to help him fully recover, Roberts said: “That’s a hard question and I understand the thought behind it. But it’s gotten better over the last few weeks, markedly. He’s been a very productive player. ... You trust him. He feels like he can go.

“He’s not 100%; very few players are 100%. Then what is it? Is it 70%, is it 80%, is it 90%? For me, there’s still that conversation, where he understands the most important part of the season is to come, and he understands his value with our team.”

It doesn’t seem like the Dodgers are ready to put Ohtani on the injured list just yet. Roberts said he hopes Ohtani will start playing catch this weekend or next week.

The Dodgers, however, had expressed hope that the injection and time off over the break would prevent Ohtani from having to manage the problem. That no longer seems to be in play.

“We’re talking about this constantly, we are,” Roberts said. “And nothing should be off the table and nothing is set in stone. So I think it’s more of how he feels. This surprised me. So now with this new information we’ve got to have new conversations.”

LOS ANGELES (AP) — Shohei Ohtani wasn't in the lineup for the Los Angeles Dodgers on Thursday night because of lingering soreness in his left knee that is keeping him off the mound.

The two-way superstar wanted to play against the Seattle Mariners, manager Dave Roberts said, but it was the team's decision to rest him. Ohtani told the training staff of renewed soreness after Wednesday night's 4-2 win.

“I appreciate the communication,” Roberts said. “I can’t read minds, the training staff can’t read minds, so just for him to communicate that then allows for us to make a decision.”

Second baseman Tommy Edman was set to bat leadoff in Ohtani’s place in the series finale.

“If there was something structural, then we would be much more concerned,” Andrew Friedman, president of baseball operations, said Wednesday. “The fact that there’s not and the fact that it does keep improving suggests that we’re on the right path.”

title: Dave Roberts Updates Shohei Ohtani’s Status Amid Knee Injury
description: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani is dealing with a knee injury, and manager Dave Roberts revealed how that injury impacts his usage.
fullText:
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani continues to lead off the batting order, but he’s recently been held out of the pitching rotation due to pain in his left knee.

His progression back to the mound was recently paused, as his expected bullpen session on Saturday was canceled due to knee pain.

With Ohtani forming a core part of the anticipated starting rotation for the playoffs, questions remain about how best to handle him the rest of the regular season.

Manager Dave Roberts recently weighed in on that question and revealed his thought process behind using Ohtani when speaking with Katie Woo of The Athletic.

Though Ohtani normally pitches only once every six games as part of the starting rotation, he plays pretty much every game at designated hitter.

So does that offensive play affect his knee?

Roberts said he spoke with Ohtani about that, and the superstar said his knee pain is unrelated to hitting.

“From his words, the hitting, the running, as he has done the last couple nights, doesn’t affect him,” Roberts told Woo. “I can only go by what he and the training staff are telling me. So, unless I hear otherwise, that hitting compromises his health, then I’m going to keep putting him in the lineup.”

Woo also reported that the Dodgers won’t push Ohtani to throw another bullpen session “until he feels 100 percent” out of fears that he could get injured even more.

“Should Ohtani rush a comeback, he risks overcompensating, which could lead to other issues not as treatable as the team believes his knee is,” Woo wrote.

And if Ohtani were to get hurt in a way that prevents him from hitting as well, that could be truly disastrous for the team’s goal of a three-peat.

After all, Roberts has admitted that the Dodgers value Ohtani more as a hitter than a pitcher.

And with hurlers like Justin Wrobleski, an All-Star this season, ready to step in as a pitcher if needed, there’s no need to rush Ohtani back to the mound.

So while this knee pain could cost Ohtani a shot at a Cy Young Award this season, it keeps everyone’s ultimate goal, a World Series, in play.

title: Dodgers to activate closer Edwin Díaz from IL on Wednesday after 3 months out
description: Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.
fullText:
Edwin Díaz, the most expensive closer in baseball, is about to return to the Los Angeles Dodgers. With hopefully better results this time.

Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Saturday the team plans to activate Díaz on Wednesday, according to AM 570's Dave Vassegh. Veteran utility man Kiké Hernández will also reportedly be activated on Tuesday.

Díaz is currently on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City and is scheduled to make one more appearance on Sunday.

Díaz joined the Dodgers on a three-year, $69 million contract in free agency last winter, making him MLB's highest-paid reliever after a standout career with the New York Mets. The early returns were less than what the Dodgers would have hoped, with seven earned runs allowed in his first six innings.

At 32 years old, Díaz struggled with his control, which wasn't above average even in the best of times. After seven appearances, the Dodgers shelved him in April due to loose bodies in his elbow.

Since then, the Dodgers have leaned on a resurgent Tanner Scott as their closer, an ironic development given they only signed Díaz after Scott's struggles in his first season on a similarly large contract. Overall, the team's bullpen ranks seventh in MLB with a 3.77 ERA.

Díaz and Hernández are two of several names the Dodgers will be hoping to re-introduce in the second half, with starting pitchers Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, reliever Blake Treinen and catcher Will Smith among those waiting in the wings.

fullText:
Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Kike Hernandez, after months on the injured list, is ready to return for the Dodgers after the end of his rehab assignment.

Hernandez has been out with a severe oblique strain, something that he picked up while coming back from elbow surgery.

At the end of the season, he opted to get elbow surgery after playing through it to play in the postseason. It left him with a long recovery, which included missing the World Baseball Classic and the start of the season.

Hernandez returned in late May, playing two games against the Rockies and looking rejuvenated at the plate, but his comeback was a short one.

The exact injury came on his left oblique, and any injury in the middle of the body can be tricky to return from.

However, manager Dave Roberts was left impressed with how quickly Hernandez healed. He thought the Puerto Rican could have come back a lot sooner, but the Dodgers have been careful with bringing him back

“Honestly, he looks normal,” Roberts said. “It’s really, I don’t want to say miraculous, but I’m really in disbelief how well he’s responded, given the injury. … Swinging, throwing, everything.

“There’s no compensation or feeling it. Certainly a quick healer. He’s working hard to get back.”

In Triple-A, Hernandez has gotten 18 at-bats, with six hits to his name, two of which were doubles, and a home run.

His swing improvements have seemingly carried over despite his injuries. He continues to look comfortable at the plate and deliver results.

With him returning, Alex Freeland is the likely roster casualty, moving back down to Triple-A.

Although there is a chance that Alex Call could be designated for assignment, Roberts and the Dodgers tend to favor his outfield versatility and baserunning.

Regardless, Hernandez unlocks a ton of flexibility, helping the Dodgers rotate at a ton of positions. More importantly, the veteran team gets the chance to totally integrate him into the picture ahead of October.

title: LA Dodgers and MVP Ohtani launch summer of live baseball on BBC

fullText:
Defending World Series champions the Los Angeles Dodgers will launch a summer of live Major League Baseball on the BBC when they meet the New York Mets on Sunday.

The Dodgers lead the National League again in 2026, with last season's Most Valuable Player, Shohei Ohtani, to the fore as they target a third consecutive World Series title.

The struggling Mets are in need of inspiration from star man Juan Soto as they look to turn around a difficult start to the season.

The game sets up a run of 10 consecutive live Sunday night MLB matches on the BBC, including the season finale on September 27 before four post-season games the following week.

Why Dodgers are on brink of World Series dynasty

The night the Tartan Army took over iconic Fenway Park

The Dodgers' record of 65 wins and 38 defeats means they are likely to win the National League West for the 13th time in 14th years.

Their recent dominance is built around Ohtani, whose achievements are now compared to the greatest players in the history of the game.

His ability to both hit and pitch at the top level consistently - he already has 22 home runs this year and has recorded eight wins as a pitcher - demonstrates a similar skill-set to the legendary two-way player Babe Ruth.

Ohtani has been named Most Valuable Player in his league four times, including last season, when the Dodgers became the first franchise in 25 years to win consecutive World Series titles.

Dominican left-fielder Soto became the highest-paid player in baseball history in 2024 when he left the New York Yankees and signed a $765m deal with their bitter cross-city rivals the Mets.

He hit his 250th career home run against the Yankees earlier this season, one of 21 home runs he has delivered in 2026.

Despite Soto's contribution, the Mets narrowly missed out on a post-season berth last year and now sit bottom of the National League East with 43 wins to 60 defeats.

title: Dave Roberts Comments on Eric Lauer’s Undefeated Record
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers are yet to lose when starter Eric Lauer pitches for them, currently boasting an 8-0 record when he pitches.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are yet to lose when starter Eric Lauer pitches for them, currently boasting an 8-0 record when the left-hander pitches.

The Dodgers traded for Lauer after the Toronto Blue Jays put him on waivers in May, and he has been a big part of a bullpen which suffered some injuries early in the season. Through his eight appearances, Lauer has a 3.35 ERA and a spotless 4-0 record.

Lauer is aware of the streak he has put together, and has let manager Dave Roberts know about his performances while showing off the confidence he’s grown.

“He’s told me,” Roberts said. “He’s told me that when he starts, we win.”

Lauer notoriously spoke out against having an opener while he played for the Blue Jays, and used his solid record with the Dodgers as leverage when the Dodgers proposed the idea. The Dodgers still went through with using an opener, having Will Klein come out before Lauer threw six no-hit innings against the Minnesota Twins.

“That was when we were discussing the opener that we used the one time (in Minnesota last month), and I just mentioned to him (Roberts) I was like, ‘Listen, we’re 4-0 when I start the game,’” Lauer said of his interaction with Roberts. “But it was more of a joke than anything.”

The southpaw pitched against the Philadelphia Phillies on Wednesday, and turned in yet another solid performance in his long list of strong showings for the Dodgers. Despite allowing three runs through 5.1 innings pitched, Lauer kept the Dodgers in the game and allowed them a chance to win. He struck out five batters in the game, matching his high with the Dodgers.

For the time being, Lauer has certainly earned his keep as a starter for the Dodgers—especially with their current injury crisis. When players start returning, though, he may make a move into the bullpen.

The Dodgers have a five-man rotation for the time being, as nobody has replaced Shohei Ohtani since the Dodgers shut him down from pitching due to his irritated knee. Blake Snell is on his way back, so he would likely fill the open slot whenever he does come back, and Ohtani would force someone out of the rotation.

That player could be Lauer depending on the team’s view on right-hander Emmet Sheehan, but the Dodgers also have a decision to make with Lauer before Aug. 3. Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic says the Dodgers could trade him at the trade deadline if their starters come back from the injured list.

“Depending on how Snell and Glasnow progress through the end of July, trading Eric Lauer — especially with several teams looking to fortify their rotations — remains a possibility,” Ardaya wrote.

While the future isn’t certain for Lauer at the moment, his strong performances are more than welcome in the Dodgers rotation for as long as he continues producing.

fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers battled the elements and made one great play to end both their game in Philadelphia and their brief two-game losing skid.

The Dodgers executed an impressive 5-2-6-4 double play that ended their 2-1 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies at a rain-soaked Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday.

The Dodgers became the first team to reach 64 wins this season and evened the three-game series after falling 10-7 to the Phillies on Monday.

Justin Wrobleski picked up his 11th victory, and Tanner Scott got five outs, and cheated death by inducing the game-ending double play, to pick up his 15th save of the season.

It all turned out well for the Dodgers but not before Scott pitched them into a huge jam in the ninth inning.

After retiring Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper to end the eighth inning, Scott gave up a single to Alec Bohm then a double to Phillies catcher J.T. Realmuto, setting the Phillies up with runners on second and third with only one out.

But Scott induced Brandon Marsh to hit a bouncer to Max Muncy, who ran at pinch runner Justin Crawford, trapping him in a rundown before throwing the ball to catcher Dalton Rushing.

https://x.com/SportsNetLA/status/2079755637383377286?s=20

“It’s just fundamentals,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Max did a great job securing the baseball and understood that the tying run was going home and secured it and ran [Crawford] hard back.”

Realmuto had reached third base but retreated back to second after Crawford went back to third. So after shortstop Mookie Betts tagged Crawford, he threw a strike to second baseman Tommy Edman, who placed a perfect tag on Realmuto, ending the game

“I knew Crawford was fast,” Scott told Spectrum Sportsnet LA. “Muncy got the ball to Rushing, and Rushing had to get it to Mookie, and next thing I know I see JT going back, and Mookie made a hell of a play.”

“That play in itself was a huge play, ended the game,” Roberts said. “Fortunately, [Realmuto] made an uncharacteristic baserunning mistake, and fortunately Mookie threw a dart to second base.”

Muncy, who also homered in the game and tied Ron Cey for second on the Dodgers’ all-time list, was more satisfied with starting the double play than making history.

“The defensive play means more to me than the homer,” Muncy said. “For me, the work I’ve been putting in on defense, anytime I can make an impact on defense, those are way more important to me.”

The Monday night game between the NL powers was sloppily played. It had 17 runs, and the Dodgers left nine on base. Phillies shortstop Trea Turner should have had three errors himself, even though he only ended the game with only one.

But even though Tuesday’s game was delayed by 1 hour and 20 minutes, it had big October vibes. Wrobleski, who pitched in Philadelphia in the All-Star Game last week, squared off against Zack Wheeler, who was named an all-star but did not participate, and each starter delivered.

Even Roberts could sense the playoff vibes which, fortunately for the Dodgers, resulted in similar fashion to last year, when LA eked out a four-game series win in the NLDS.

“That was a playoff environment,” Roberts said. “I think you can tell how badly we wanted it, how bad they wanted it. You’ve got two heavyweight teams going toe to toe, and we didn’t give anything away. I was really proud of the way we competed tonight.”

title: Dodgers make first trade deadline move, pick up injured reliever Seth Halvorsen from Rockies
description: Seth Halvorsen is still looking for success in the majors.
fullText:
In need of help with the MLB trade deadline fast approaching, the Los Angeles Dodgers got ahead of other teams and made a move a few days before trade talks really heat up. The team reportedly acquired injured reliever Seth Halvorsen from the Colorado Rockies on Monday in exchange for two minor-league players, per multiple reports.

Halvorsen, 26, has a 4.74 ERA over 19 innings with the Rockies this season.

Seth Halvorsen goes to Dodgers from Rockies for prospects Nick Frasso and Landyn Vidourek

— Jon Heyman (@JonHeyman) July 20, 2026

On the surface, the Halvorsen acquisition is strange for a few reasons. First off, it’s an inter-division deal, with two teams in the National League West coming together to exchange players. Neither the Rockies of Dodgers likely feel too strongly about the pieces surrendered in the deal, as inter-division trades could come back to haunt one team if a player emerges as a future superstar.

Whether Halvorsen can leap into that role depends on what the Dodgers plan to do with the reliever. In his brief MLB appearances, Halvorsen hasn’t been impressive. He holds a career 4.31 ERA, with a 21.0 percent strikeout rate and 12.1 walk rate. Since Halvorsen made his MLB debut in 2024, relievers have averaged a higher strikeout rate and lower walk rate than Halvorsen.

Things have gotten particularly rough for Halvorsen this season, as he’s issued nearly as many walks as strikeouts in his 19 innings in the majors.

On top of that, Halvorsen is currently injured. The reliever is in the middle of a rehab assignment due to shoulder inflammation. He’ll continue that assignment with the Dodgers. Once the team deems him ready, it will need to decide whether to promote Halvorsen to the majors or keep him in the minors.

While the Dodgers are in the midst of yet another excellent year, the team’s one weakness — if you can even call it that — is its bullpen. Los Angeles’ offense ranks first in the majors in wRC+ — an advanced stat that measures a offensive performance. The team also ranks first in MLB with a 3.36 ERA from its starting pitchers. It’s bullpen ranks seventh with a 3.71 ERA.

While that’s hardly a major reason for concern, the Dodgers are at least trying to remedy some issues by acquiring a reliever ahead of the deadline. On the surface, Halvorsen doesn’t seem that exciting, but the Dodgers are known for having a strong player-development system, and could have changes in mind to help Halvorsen take a step forward.

Prior to 2026, Halvorsen posted strong Stuff+ numbers, suggesting his pitches are nasty enough to be successful in the majors. But his control and command have always lagged behind, something borne out in the advanced stats and the eye test.

The two prospects the team shipped out for Halvorsen — Nick Frasso and Landyn Vidourek — could wind up playing a role for the Rockies moving forward. While Frasso was once a top-100 prospect, he’s now 27 and has never appeared in the majors. But that could change soon, as the Rockies could always use pitching.

Vidourek is a 22-year-old outfielder who the Dodgers selected in the third round of the 2025 MLB Draft. He posted strong numbers last season, but has seen his batting average dip below .200 in the minors in 2026. If either prospect is going to make the Dodgers regret the deal, it’s likely Vidourek, who is still young and has shown some ability in the minors already.

Given the Dodgers’ seemingly endless supply of talented players, the Halvorsen acquisition may not even rate as a notable transaction by the team by season’s end. With Edwin Diaz working his way back from injury, the team’s bullpen is set to get a boost before long. Additionally, the Halvorsen deal doesn’t prevent the team from making a more substantial acquisition in its bullpen before the trade deadline passes.

If Halvorsen does play a significant role with the team down the stretch, it will likely be due to the Dodgers unlocking something with the reliever. If he doesn’t, it’s unlikely to affect the Dodgers in any way. The team will almost certainly make higher-profile moves at the deadline and can afford to miss on a player or two given the immense talent already present within the organization.

title: Grangeville's Adkison, WSU's Manzardo highlight local connections to pro baseball
description: Jul. 18—When a door closes, another may open. fullText:
Jul. 18—When a door closes, another may open.

That's exactly what happened for 2019 Grangeville High School graduate Chase Adkison when he signed with the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers' organization in June.

Following a long-term injury to Dodgers All-Star catcher Will Smith, L.A. initiated a chain reaction of catcher promotions and signings, eventually finding Adkison, recently released by the St. Louis Cardinals' organization.

Adkison reported to the Dodgers' High-A affiliate, the Great Lakes Loons in Midland, Mich, where through 13 games he has nine hits, five walks, a double, four RBI and nine runs.

In parts of four seasons in minor league baseball, Adkison is batting .268, with five home runs, 55 RBI and 56 runs.

The Grangeville grad found his way to professional baseball by way of the now-defunct Boise State baseball program in 2020, San Jacinto College (Texas) in 2021 and two standout seasons at Oklahoma State, where he started 98 total games and batted .282, with 11 home runs, 16 doubles, a triple, 41 walks, 69 RBI and 77 runs.

"This move is another opportunity to continue playing professional baseball," Adkison said in an Idaho County Free Press article. "I'm excited to be wearing a new uniform and have the chance to compete every day. I'm grateful for the opportunity and looking forward to helping the organization however I can."

Adkison holds four Grangeville High baseball records seven years after his career concluded, including single-season batting average (.653), single-season triples (eight), career hits (151) and career triples (20), according to the Idaho County Free Press.

Here's a look at other local connections to major and minor league baseball in 2026, including 10 Washington State Cougars and four Lewis-Clark State Warriors.

Connor Brogdon — RHP — Cleveland Guardians

With the Angels last season, Connor Brogdon signed in December with the Cleveland Guardians.

In 15 appearances, Brogdon has turned in a 2-2 record and 5.28 ERA. He has struck out 14 through 15 1/3 innings.

Seth Brown — OF — New York Yankees — Triple-A

Weeks before shuttling off to Florida for spring training, MLB veteran Seth Brown visited his alma mater Lewis-Clark State for a first-of-its-kind fundraising dinner.

The favor benefited his college coach, Jeremiah Robbins, who returned to LCSC this past season.

Brown spoke about how his time in Lewiston springboarded him to the career he has had. After seven years with the Athletics, Brown signed with the New York Yankees this past winter and is waiting for his opportunity.

With the Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, Brown has logged 53 games and is batting .235, with 43 hits, including six doubles, a triple and nine home runs en route to 21 RBI and 23 runs.

Drake George — RHP — San Francisco Giants — Single-A

After turning in a 3.20 ERA in Year 1, Drake George has been on the Giants org's injured list for the entire season so far.

Last year, George struck out 62 through 56 1/3 innings pitched.

Jadon Williamson — RHP — Miami Marlins — FCL Marlins

The most recent Warrior-turned-pro-baseball player on this list, Jadon Williamson has gotten two starts and made 11 total appearances for the Florida Complex League Marlins in 2026 after being selected in the 11th round of the 2025 MLB draft.

Williamson holds a 15.66 ERA, but he has struck out 24 batters through 16 2/3 innings pitched.

Kyle Manzardo — 1B/DH — Cleveland Guardians

WSU's former star slugger Kyle Manzardo has had a so-so year at the plate in 2026, but what transpired in his life over a year ago dwarfs any sort of success or failure he could experience between the lines.

In July 2025, Manzardo's mother, Windy Manzardo, underwent long-awaited heart transplant surgery. Kyle Manzardo flew from Houston, where the Cleveland Guardians had just arrived, to Spokane to be with his mother.

The surgery was a success, and since then, Windy and Kyle's father, Paul Manzardo, have gotten to watch their son live without the cloud of Windy's condition hanging over their lives.

"I guess now that it's over, I've kind of realized how heavy that was to just be carrying it around with you for a couple of years now," Kyle Manzardo said via MLB.com. "Just grateful it's hopefully done with now."

At the All-Star break, Manzardo was batting .215 through 87 games with seven doubles, one triple, 10 home runs and 30 RBI along with 32 runs scored for the 51-46 Cleveland Guardians, a half a game back from the Chicago White Sox in the American League Central division as of Friday.

Ryan Walker — RHP — San Francisco Giants

Joining Manzardo as one of two Cougs actively in the majors, Ryan Walker has remained a fixture of the San Francisco Giants bullpen.

However, he saw an early role as closer fade away after three saves to three blown saves. With 26 1/3 innings pitched through 27 appearances, Walker has posted a 7.52 ERA with 19 strikeouts to 15 walks.

Ian Hamilton — RHP — Atlanta Braves — Triple-A

Ian Hamilton spent the last three years in the big leagues with the New York Yankees. He signed with the Atlanta Braves' org in the offseason and, in four big-league appearances with the Braves, allowed four earned runs on six hits.

In 22 appearances for Triple-A Gwinnett, Hamilton has pitched 23 2/3 innings and is 2-0 with four saves, two holds, 30 strikeouts and a 3.04 ERA.

Brandon White — RHP — Miami Marlins — Triple-A

From Chehalis, Wash., Brandon White has been working his way up the Miami Marlins' farm system ranks since the club drafted him out of WSU in 2021.

This year with the Triple-A Jacksonville Jumbo Shrimp, White has pitched 71 2/3 innings with 16 appearances and 14 starts. He has struck out 87 batters and posted a 4.40 ERA.

Jonah Advincula — OF — Cleveland Guardians — Double-A

After starting the season injured, Jonah Advincula has joined Double-A Akron for nine games, going 9-for-28 at the plate with three doubles, three home runs, four stolen bases and 10 runs scored.

Sam Brown — INF — Washington Nationals — Double-A

Acquired by the Nationals as part of a July 30, 2025, trade with the Angels, Brown is hitting .238 with 49 hits through 56 games. He has 11 doubles, three home runs, 17 RBI and 19 runs.

Zane Mills — RHP — Chicago Cubs — Double-A

Before suffering a season-ending knee injury, Zane Mills made one appearance for Double-A Knoxville in the Chicago Cubs' organization.

Dakota Hawkins — RHP — New York Mets — High-A

Dakota Hawkins made one appearance each in the Double-A and Triple-A levels of the New York Mets' org, but has settled in with High-A Brooklyn, where through 17 appearances he is 3-0 with two holds, a 2.54 ERA and 33 strikeouts.

Will Cresswell — C — Toronto Blue Jays — Single-A

Cresswells's last 12 months have been eventful. The WSU's most-recent pro wrapped up the 2025 season in Pullman and was drafted by the Toronto Blue Jays in July 2025. He spent March representing Great Britain in the World Baseball Classic.

With the Blue Jays' Single-A affiliate, Creswell has played in 34 games and notched 23 hits, including three doubles, a home run along with 15 RBI and 11 runs.

Connor Wilford — RHP — Seattle Mariners — ACL

Connor Wilford started the year with Lexington of the Atlantic League, an independent baseball league, before the Seattle Mariners purchased his contract. Now with the Arizona Complex League Mariners, Wilford is off to a fast start, making four starts in five appearances for a 2-1 record, 2.45 ERA and 27 strikeouts through 22 innings.

While not associated with an MLB organization, left-handed pitcher A.J. Block and catcher Jacob Morrow play in independent leagues. Block hurls for a Lake County (Wis.) team, while Morrow plays for a Lincoln (Neb.) squad.

Block was with the Angels' Double-A affiliate last season and pitched 14 games for Durango in the Mexican League, recording 14 strikeouts through 8 2/3 innings.

title: Brewers Lose Starting Outfielder To Shoulder Injury As Race With Dodgers Heats Up
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers are the only teams in baseball with at least 60 wins
fullText:
There are only two teams in baseball with at least 60 wins, and they could not be built more differently.

The Los Angeles Dodgers enter play on Saturday at 62-36 with one of the highest payrolls in baseball and an array of All-Stars. Meanwhile, the Brewers are right behind them at 60-37, with a low payroll and a roster built through the draft and reclamation projects. However, just as the race for the top seed in the National League heats up, the Brewers have lost starting right fielder Sal Frelick to a shoulder injury.

Frelick threw a ball in on a double by Otto Lopez in the fourth inning, but the throw was well short and bounced into Brice Turang. Frelick has a great arm so it was a sign that something was wrong. He was pulled from the game in the following inning.

"Sal tried to make a throw in the outfield and he felt it," manager Pat Murphy said after the game. "He's had a little issue earlier this season. We don't want to take any chances... I suspect he won't be able to go anytime soon. That's what it looks like."

Do you have a take to get off your chest? Do you want to engage in a growing Brewers community? Comment on our content alongside staff and fans alike!

Frelick was great last season, but has not been as sharp at the plate this year. He was starting to heat up after putting together a phenomenal month of June. However, he will now spend some time on the shgelp. Luckily for the Brewers, they have plenty of options to replace him. For starters, Luis Lara could see regular starts now. The Brewers called him up before the All-Star break. He is one of their top prospects and has already signed an extension with the team.

The injury could also pave the way for Jake Bauers to see more time in the outfield and for Andrew Vaughn to finally become a regular starter again. Vaughn has actually been one of the Brewers best hitters, but Bauers has been so hot at the plate, the team has had no choice but to have the two share first base.

title: Dodgers Announce Long-Awaited Bobblehead of Iconic World Series Moment
description: The Dodgers, following a good deal of fan demand, finally announced a bobblehead honoring Andy Pages' iconic World Series Game 7 catch.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers, following a good deal of fan demand, finally announced a bobblehead honoring Andy Pages’ iconic World Series Game 7 catch.

The Dodgers have one of the best, if not the best, bobblehead promotions every year, but this one holds special meaning for fans who took in the World Series.

Coined “The Catch” bobblehead, it will be given to fans on September 6th against the Washington National.

The bobblehead captures the moment where Andy Pages rises up for a catch on a fly ball in between left and center field, while Kike Hernandez ducks under and lets him make the catch.

Both players had a big collision, but Hernandez took the brunt of it. Hernandez got up happy after finding out Pages made the catch.

In the collectible, Hernandez looks quite funny as he seemingly accepts getting run over by Pages, and honestly, it is not too dissimilar from how the moment actually happened.

The play is already incredible from Pages in any context, but with the context of it being Game 7 of a World Series, with the bases loaded in the bottom of the ninth inning with two outs, the moment takes on its own legend.

It was all the more special since Pages had been in an awful slump, failing to hit any pitch that came his way. He came in as a defensive substitute late in the game and pulled out a gutsy, iconic, and terrifying catch all in one go.

Based on recent bobbleheads, this collectible should end up going past $100. Kike Hernandez’s pitching bobblehead, which came out very recently, resells for around $75.

“The Catch,” considering everything about the moment and what it means in modern Dodgers history, should blow well past that.

It does not have the mainstream appeal of Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s Yoshi bobblehead, which goes for $170, but for any hardcore Dodgers fan, “The Catch” bobblehead is a must-have and will be in demand.

The get-in price is around $165 as of Wednesday, July 15th.
